senses.gloss: f. (נגד, נ absorbed or dropped = הַגָּדָה) tale, story, lesson, esp. Agadah, that class of Rabb. literature which explains the Bible homiletically, opp. to Halakhah or legal interpretation (הֲלָכָה, שְׁמוּעָה).
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 23a">M. Kat. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>שמ׳ וא׳</he> a legal tradition and an Agadah (homily).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 6:2:3">Y. B. Bath. VI, 15ᶜ</cite> <he>מסורת א׳ היא</he> it is a traditional Agadah.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:2:4">Y. Git. IV, 45ᶜ</cite> <he>בא׳ … מאן דייק לן</he> who among us can enter into what thy grandfather said?—<he>בעל א׳</he> a lecturer on Agadah.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 94:5">Gen. R. s. 94</cite>; a. fr.—<he>אֲגָּדַת תלים</he> the Agadah on Psalms.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 22:1">Lev. R. s. 22</cite>, beg.; a. fr.—Cmp. <cite ref="A00253"><he>אֲגַדְתָּא</he></cite>.
